title: Stellar feedback in M83 as observed with MUSE. I. Overview, an unprecedented view of the stellar and gas kinematics and evidence of outflowing gas
question: How do the kinematics of stars, ionised gas, and molecular gas compare in M83 at ~20 pc scales, and what is the fraction and ionisation mechanism of diffuse ionised gas and central outflow/inflow structures?

data.sensitivity: rms brightness temperature sensitivity of 0.17 K

evidence.loc: Introduction
evidence.quote: M83 (also known in the literature as NGC 5236) is a nearby spiral galaxy, at a distance of 4.89 Mpc (cite: jacobs09).

what.value: Effective radius, stellar mass, SFR, main sequence offset, and molecular depletion time of M83; PHANGS-ALMA CO(2-1) data products

evidence.loc: Introduction
evidence.quote: The galaxy has a stellar mass $\log_{10} M_\star = 10.53 M_\odot$ (cite: leroy21) and hosts a nuclear starburst ring (cite: sersic65; buta93; calzetti04; knapen10; comeron10), resulting in a high star formation rate (SFR = 4.2 $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$, (cite: leroy21)).

evidence.loc: Dataset overview and MUSE data reduction
evidence.quote: The data are described in detail in (cite: leroy21), and the data reduction in (cite: leroy21_pipeline).

evidence.loc: Dataset overview and MUSE data reduction

(1) in (cite: sun20) and assuming a CO(2–1)-to-CO(1–0) line ratio $R_{21} = 0.65$ (cite: denbrok21_alma; leroy21_subm) and a standard Galactic CO-to-H2 conversion factor $\alpha_{\rm CO} = 4.35$ $M_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$ (K km s$^{-1}$)$^{-1}$, these values corresponds to a cold gas surface density of $\simeq 30$ and 170 $M_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$.

recipe.goal: Reduce MUSE observations and assemble the 26-pointing mosaic
recipe.method: Standard ESO MUSE pipeline reduction, sky subtraction with 'subtract-model', exposure alignment, and pointing alignment to HST B-band mosaic registered to Gaia DR2
key_parameters: subtract-model sky subtraction method; Moffat PSF fit

recipe.goal: Derive stellar, ionised gas, and molecular gas kinematics and fit 2D rotation models
recipe.method: Voronoi binning and PPXF fitting for stellar continuum; single and double Gaussian fitting (with BIC selection) for H-alpha in continuum-subtracted cube; PHANGS-ALMA mom1/mom2 maps and Gaussian fits to CO spectra; 2D double-Plummer rotation curve fitting with MocKinG
key_parameters: Stellar Voronoi S/N ~ 250 in 5025-5065 A, fit range 4600-8740 A (excluding 7220-8507 A)
H-alpha Voronoi S/N ~ 20, fit window 22 A (+/- 500 km s^-1)
2D kinematic fit angular sector of inclusion = 67.5 degrees around major axis with cosine weighting
assumptions: CO(2-1)-to-CO(1-0) line ratio R_21 = 0.65 and alpha_CO = 4.35 M_sun pc^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1

recipe.goal: Estimate dust extinction, separate HII regions from DIG, and perform BPT diagram analysis
recipe.method: Compute E(B-V) from H-beta/H-alpha ratio using PYNEB and compare with ALMA CO surface density; separate HII regions and DIG using ASTRODENDRO and [SII]/H-alpha cut; analyse BPT emission line ratios against star formation limits and shock models
key_parameters: ASTRODENDRO min leaf size = 4.3 pixels (0.86''), min_delta = 0, SB threshold = 1.23e-15 erg s^-1 cm^-2 arcsec^-2; alternative cut [SII] 6716,31/H-alpha = 0.29
assumptions: Intrinsic H-alpha/H-beta = 2.863 (case B recombination, T_e = 10^4 K, n_e = 100 cm^-3) and Cardelli et al. (1989) extinction law; T_e ~ 10000 K and n_e = 10^3 cm^-3 for H-alpha luminosity threshold

evidence.quote: The resulting $f_{\rm DIG}$ ratio is shown in black in Fig. [7](#fig:fdig_vs_r); we see that the DIG contribution to the total luminosity varies between 0.8% and 46%, peaking in the interarm region.

answer_key.quantity: Photoionisation fraction of H-alpha flux in H II regions

evidence.loc: BPT diagram analysis
evidence.quote: We observe that, as expected, in H ii regions SF accounts for most of the H$\alpha$ flux (99.8% of the flux originates from regions where photoionisation is the dominant mechanism), whereas bins classified as DIG have a mixed contribution from both photoionisation-dominated regions (accounting for 94.9% of the flux) and shock-dominated regions (accounting for the remaining 5.1%).
